title: Data Center Network: Layer-by-Layer Broadcast Log
description:
You are an infrastructure engineer at a cloud company. Your data center uses a hierarchical tree topology where a root switch fans out to aggregation switches, which in turn fan out to rack-level switches, and so on. During a routine diagnostic, you need to generate a broadcast log that records which switch IDs received a signal at each "hop" level from the root.

Given a binary tree representing the switch hierarchy (where each node stores the switch's integer ID), return a 2D list where each inner list contains the switch IDs at that depth level, ordered from left to right. Each line of output should represent one level of the hierarchy. If the tree is empty, output nothing.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000].
Node values (switch IDs) are in the range [-1000, 1000].
The tree is given as a level-order serialization using -1 to represent null/missing child nodes.
input_format: A single line containing space-separated integers representing the binary tree in level-order (BFS) serialization. The value -1 denotes a null node (no switch at that position). An empty line or the single token -1 means the tree is empty.
output_format: Print one line per level of the tree. Each line contains the space-separated switch IDs at that level from left to right. If the tree is empty, print nothing.

test_cases.purpose: Typical balanced tree with 3 levels — standard base case
Empty tree — edge case with no nodes
All duplicate values — perfect binary tree with 4 levels, tests repeated IDs
Left-skewed tree — would reveal O(n²) performance issues with naive solutions
Full binary tree with 4 levels — checks correct left-to-right ordering across all levels
Tree with negative switch IDs — validates handling of negative values
